recommendations.title: Enable a controlled single-entry route into the legacy quote system
recommendations.description: The reported process has Sales record quote data in Excel and John re-enter it in the legacy quote system. Assess whether a structured intake, import, or integration can carry the data forward without re-keying. Do not assume the legacy system supports these options; if it does not, retain the current entry process until an approved alternative is available.
recommendations.proposed_automation: Subject to feasibility and approval, let Sales submit quote data once through an approved structured intake. Validate required fields and route the submission to John or an authorized reviewer. If a supported import or integration exists, use it to populate the legacy quote system; otherwise provide a controlled handoff that avoids implying data has been entered automatically.
recommendations.human_control: John or an authorized reviewer verifies the quote data and resolves validation issues before confirming the legacy-system record. Sales remains responsible for the accuracy of submitted quote details.
dependencies: Confirm whether the legacy quote system supports a suitable import, interface, or integration.

Agree on ownership for data corrections and failed submissions.
risks: An import or integration may not be technically supported.

The reviewer confirms successful entry or records an issue for correction and follow-up.

recommendations.title: Transfer quote data from Excel to the legacy system with human review
recommendations.description: Assess and, if technically feasible, configure a controlled transfer from Sales' Excel quote record to the legacy quote system. The transfer could use an available import or integration mechanism; the supplied information does not establish that either system supports this. John should review the transferred data and resolve errors before finalizing it in the legacy system.
recommendations.proposed_automation: Subject to confirming system capabilities, automatically route or transfer the Excel quote data to a review queue or supported import process, reducing the need for John to re-enter the same fields. If direct transfer is not supported, assess a standardized file-based import as an alternative; do not assume that this is available.
recommendations.human_control: John reviews the transferred data, resolves exceptions, and decides whether it is ready to be finalized in the legacy system. Sales remains responsible for the accuracy of the original quote information.
dependencies: Confirm whether the legacy quote system and Excel workflow support a safe import, integration, or other controlled transfer.
Agree on quote-field mappings, required fields, exception handling, and who owns corrections.
Decide whether the existing email handoff should be replaced by a controlled queue or retained alongside the transfer.
risks: An unverified field mapping or incompatible format could transfer incomplete or incorrect quote data.
If the systems do not support a suitable transfer method, the proposed reduction in re-entry may not be feasible as described.
Changing the handoff channel without an agreed process could cause quotes or exceptions to be missed.

to_be_steps.description: Sales records the quote in Excel, as in the reported current process.

If a supported transfer mechanism is confirmed and configured, the quote data is routed or made available to John for review without re-entering the same fields. The handoff mechanism remains subject to an organizational decision.

John checks the transferred data, handles discrepancies or missing information, and finalizes the quote in the legacy system. If transfer is unavailable, the current manual-entry step remains until an alternative is agreed.

retained_human_decisions: Sales determines and verifies the quote information recorded in Excel.
John judges whether transferred information is complete and accurate enough to finalize in the legacy system.
The organization decides whether and how to replace or modify the email handoff.
assumptions: The supplied description is reported practice from a user claim, not evidence of documented policy or procedure.
A supported data-transfer or import method may be possible, but this is unverified and is not treated as an existing system capability.
The design retains the reported Sales-to-John sequence and does not assume that the Excel step can be removed.

verifications.explanation: The user-reported evidence supports the current Excel-to-email-to-John process and duplicate manual entry. It does not establish that Excel or the legacy quote system supports a safe import, integration, or controlled transfer, or that the proposed field mappings and exception process are workable. The recommendation appropriately makes implementation conditional on confirming feasibility, but the transfer approach and its expected reduction in re-entry remain unverified.
